checks: Migration executes twice on PostgreSQL and registers one named five-minute cleanup job in the cron fixture.
Fresh transmission receipts survive cleanup so UI reads, acknowledgement retries and request retries remain valid.
All four old terminal statuses are deleted while the AC result, desired OFF, latest remote OFF and controller registration stay intact.
A late ACK after cleanup keeps a valid ESP32 connected without recreating a command; cross-device and missing-ID ACKs remain denied.
Valid queued and claimed commands survive cleanup, including an old-created row whose expiry is still in the future.
Offline overdue commands become expired with a readable failure receipt and matching queued AC requests become Failed.
Expiry of an older command cannot fail a newer AC request.
Anonymous devices and browser users cannot call the owner-only cleanup routine.
Only old completed runs for this cleanup job are pruned; unrelated and running cron jobs stay intact.
Large backlogs drain in bounded batches and repeated cleanup remains safe.
cron_execution: Catalog/schedule fixture; real pg_cron deployment still required
